description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai unveiled new educational features tailored for students. These enhancements are designed to facilitate topic comprehension and exam preparation. Gemini now includes a specialized student hub, complete with study notebooks and various learning tools. Furthermore, eligible college students can access free subscriptions to Google AI Pro or Plus, alongside bundled discounts for AI Pro and YouTube Premium.
title: CEO Sundar Pichai has a quiz for students about Google Search

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Two children's bodies were recovered from an irrigation canal after their father allegedly pushed them. The nine-year-old girl and her two-and-a-half-year-old brother were found during a search operation. Police received an emergency call from the father, Shantappa, who was with his six-year-old daughter. He reportedly stated the deceased children were closer to their mother and did not get along with him.
title: Karnataka: Father 'pushes' 2 children into canal for favouring mother, both die

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: During a turbulent Khasi Students' Union bike rally in Shillong, statues were defaced and government vehicles set ablaze, highlighting the escalating agitation over a five-point charter of demands. Their protest also aimed at opposing a public hearing for a proposed limestone mining project. This rally was marked by an ultimatum issued by the union prior to the symbolic black-flag demonstration, reflecting their deep-seated grievances.
title: Statues vandalised, vehicles torched after students rally turns violent in Meghalaya

author: TOI SPORTS DESK
description: In a stunning debut, Manav Suthar has made history as the first spinner to secure five wickets in both his first home and away Tests, a remarkable achievement not seen since Mohammad Nisar in 1933. At just a young age, he also became the youngest Indian to claim ten wickets in a single Test match, eclipsing Harbhajan Singh's previous record.
title: Manav Suthar scripts history, equals 93-year-old Indian Test record

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Indian authorities removed the external security cordon around the Pakistan High Commission. Traffic bollards and barricades were dismantled from the diplomatic compound premises. This action effectively eliminated the external security perimeter outside the high commission. The Pakistan High Commission is situated within the Chanakyapuri diplomatic enclave.
title: Delhi removes Pak high commission's barricades after similar gesture by Islamabad

author: TNN
description: Two Class 10 students were apprehended for the murder of principal Roopa Reddy. Police allege the students killed her after she caught one stealing from her home. Investigators noticed the students spending money lavishly after the murder occurred. Forensic examination detected blood traces on cash recovered from one student. The juveniles have been produced before the Juvenile Justice Board for further proceedings.
title: Hyderabad principal stabbed 27 times: How last ‘babu’ call exposed Class 10 killers

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Millinocket, Maine, once thrived around Great Northern Paper Company, but the mill’s 2008 closure transformed the community. In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.
title: After paper mill closure, Millinocket, Maine bets on tourism and new industry

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Peyton Watson, 23, leaves the Denver Nuggets for the Cleveland Cavaliers in a mid-August sign-and-trade also touching the Clippers, Wizards and Kings. Cleveland sends out Max Strus and Tre Mann while adding Watson and forward Cam Whitmore. Watson signs a four-year, $88 million contract with a player option and trade kicker, joining Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen in Cleveland's projected starting five.
title: NBA trade news: Cleveland Cavaliers secure $88 million star in 5-team trade

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Max Lederer Jr., the publisher of Stars and Stripes, has stepped down amidst disputes over editorial independence. The Pentagon's push for more oversight has sparked tension regarding the military newspaper's objective reporting. Their recent pieces on poor conditions and declining morale reportedly led to criticism from the Department of Defense, prompting the ousting of the ombudsman who protected editorial freedom.
title: US military newspaper publisher quits amid Pentagon row over editorial freedom

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: The unexpected death of Hayden Panettiere on August 16 has prompted a thorough investigation, now involving the Drug Enforcement Administration. While the coroner's office has yet to establish an official cause of death, there were mentions of overdose and cardiac arrest during the emergency call. Known for her candid discussions about addiction and mental health, Panettiere's passing raises significant concerns.
title: DEA to investigate Hayden Panettiere’s sudden passing

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: Oil prices have settled at elevated levels, staying above ninety dollars per barrel. Investors are weighing the unpredictable US-Iran situation and the potential impacts on shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. While intermittent Middle East assaults bolster market sentiment, the absence of further escalations keeps a lid on price surges. Additionally, the UAE's suspension of financial transactions with Iran has raised regional tensions.
title: Oil price today: Crude remains above $90 as Hormuz operations remain disrupted

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Udaipur’s Chandrajeet Singh Rajawat turned a difficult childhood passion for chess into a successful career. He left home as a teenager, faced financial struggles, slept at railway stations and stadiums, and kept playing despite setbacks. His persistence eventually brought recognition, coaching opportunities and his own academy, Kingdom of Chess, which now operates across around 30 countries.
title: Gave up IIT, slept on roads: How Rajasthan's 1st AGM put Udaipur on global chess map

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are set to visit Britain later this month, bringing along their children, Archie and Lilibet, who will soon attend a British school. King Charles is eager for the chance to reconnect with his grandchildren in a private setting. Since taking a step back from royal responsibilities in March 2020, the dynamics between the couple and the royal family remain intricate and challenging.
title: No royal role for Sussexes: King Charles 'welcomes' Harry, Meghan’s UK 'return'

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Haverfordwest Castle in Pembrokeshire, Wales, is undergoing a £17.7 million transformation designed to turn the 800-year-old fortress into a major tourist attraction. The project will feature an immersive visitor centre, café, local shop, Christmas markets and a 500-seat outdoor events space. The castle is expected to reopen in 2028 with free entry for visitors.
title: £17.7m revamp planned for 800-year-old Haverfordwest Castle, reopening in 2028

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A talented high school student has pioneered a cutting-edge bioengineering method for the early detection of pancreatic cancer. By utilizing magnetic beads to isolate tumor-derived particles from blood samples, her clinical trials demonstrated remarkable accuracy. Her extraordinary research has secured her a spot as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition, offering a promising new avenue for timely diagnosis and improved patient survival outcomes.
title: Meet Audrey Zheng, 17, who developed a pancreatic cancer test

description: NCERT has recast the team for preparing political science textbooks for Classes XI and XII, with one of the two books slated to be ready by Nov. The 20-member panel includes faculty from JNU, DU, IGNOU and NLU Delhi, among others. At least four members have links, past or present, with organisations associated with RSS-BJP.

description: India will have five key matches on Day 4 of the BWF World Championships. Ayush Shetty faces Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan, while PV Sindhu takes on China’s Wang Zhi Yi. Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand Pullela, Dhruv Kapila-Tanisha Crasto and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty will also compete in the Round of 16, keeping India’s campaign busy.

description: A fake CBI raid was foiled at a Delhi businessman's residence in Rohini.  The businessman's wife refused entry to individuals claiming to be CBI officers.  These individuals then left after neighbors questioned their authorization.  The family reported the incident and submitted evidence to the police.  Police are now examining CCTV footage and investigating the matter.

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: A groundbreaking six-decade study reveals that passive rewilding effectively fosters the development of lush native woodlands. Through protective thorny scrub, young trees thrived, shielded from herbivores, while wind and jays ingeniously spread seeds, outlining the woodlands’ unique patterns. After fifty years, the area began to mirror the characteristics of ancient woodlands, showcasing an eco-friendly and budget-friendly approach to achieving woodland restoration objectives.
title: British barley field left in 1961 became woodland in 60 years

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In 1968, the introduction of opossum shrimp into Montana's lakes triggered a dramatic decline in the kokanee salmon population. The shrimp fiercely competed with young salmon for essential zooplankton, resulting in a disarrayed food chain. Meanwhile, the lake trout population thrived as they turned to the remaining salmon for sustenance. This shift irrevocably changed Flathead Lake's ecological landscape and impacted its indigenous fish communities.
title: 1968 Montana shrimp stocking led to salmon collapse and lost food for eagles and bears

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.
title: 1963 rotating house by California builder hits market for first time

author: TNN
description: Six people died and twenty-five were hospitalized after drinking methanol-spiked liquor.  The incident occurred in Bhavnagar district, with victims consuming liquor from Royal Stag bottles.  Questions arose regarding alleged police reporting delays, prompting an investigation by the State Monitoring Cell.  Patients reported breathlessness and vision loss, with officials warning of kidney complications.  The liquor was manufactured and sold locally in Bhavnagar, and suspects have been detained.
title: In dry Gujarat, spurious booze kills 6 at party thrown by cop; 25 in hospital

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.
title: 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire as species returns to UK waters
